reason: E1 directly supports precipitate formation and strength evolution during 750 °C aging in a related HEA, but the cited evidence does not address lattice strain reduction, radiation tolerance, cryogenic toughness, or the specific over-aging effects on toughness and coherency claimed in the hypothesis.
premises: Aging at 750 °C produces coherent nanoscale precipitates (e.g., γ′-type) in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
These precipitates block dislocation and defect motion, improving high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Over-aging leads to precipitate coarsening, loss of coherency, and impaired toughness.
The mechanism applies broadly to Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
